components.claim: Both grapple shots from a moving car hit and hold in the truck's windshield frame and cab
components.reasoning: A hand-fired grapple from one moving vehicle into another at close range is aimable; the uncertain part is that the hook both penetrates and anchors. Judgment prior: roughly 1 in 3 to 1 in 30 per attempt.

components.dependence: Conditional on c1 (the line holds). Independent of the drivers' pace matching, which is ordinary.

components.reasoning: NHTSA all-crash curves at an assumed 60-80 mph delta-V: survive 0.46-1.68 MU, walk away 1.63-2.91 MU. Dom is hurt but functional, so the central sits between the two curves at 70 mph (1.0 and 2.3), then +0.5 because the curves describe 2010-2015 cars with airbags and the Charger (1970) has neither airbags nor crumple zones.

components.claim: Brian hits the moving leaf at a speed and line that clears the gap without a calibrated ramp
components.reasoning: At 60+ m/s a short gap is cleared almost regardless of angle; the risk is the leaf angle changing during the approach, which makes the take-off unrepeatable. Judgment prior around 1 in 10.

components.dependence: Conditional on c1 (the car is airborne on a survivable line).
components.reasoning: Production jump cars are reinforced; street cars typically break suspension or burst tyres on landing. A rival car does exactly that in the draft screenplay, which is not evidence about the released film. Judgment prior around 1 in 10.

components.claim: An uncalibrated ramp launch lands the car on a moving boat's deck (target roughly 8 m x 5 m)
components.reasoning: Worked as stated, this model is generous, not harsh: range and timing errors of about +/-5 m each sum to a triangular spread on +/-10 m, and landing within +/-4 m of an 8 m deck is 1 - (6/10)^2 = 0.64, i.e. 0.2 MU. The real uncertainty is the ramp itself, whose angle and the boat's speed no source gives, so the scatter cannot be grounded. Held as a judgment prior of about 1 in 10.

components.claim: The yacht's deck stops a 1.5 t car without the car punching through or tumbling into the water
components.dependence: Conditional on c1 (the car reaches the deck).
components.reasoning: Leisure-yacht decks are not rated for a vehicle landing. Judgment prior around 1 in 10.

components.claim: Both occupants survive the landing and fight within minutes (one broken arm)
components.dependence: Conditional on c2; one component for both occupants (correlated outcomes).
components.reasoning: A deck landing stops the car from perhaps 30-50 mph. NHTSA all-crash curve at 40 mph gives 0.03 MU for survival, and walking away at 40 mph is 0.50 MU; a broken arm is MAIS 2, so the central is between the two. No airbags in a 1969 car.

components.claim: Two Chargers generate enough pulling force to drag a 20-40 t steel vault
components.reasoning: Sliding steel on asphalt needs at least 0.3 x m x g: 59 kN for a 20 t vault. Two Chargers can push at most about 17 kN before their tyres spin. The requirement exceeds tyre grip by 3-7x, so this is a hard-limit violation, capped at the Record Horizon. The production confirms the limit: it cut a shot of the vault hanging off the bridge because "even the powerful Chargers would not be able to support the vault's weight".

components.claim: The cars stay controllable while a mass 10-20x heavier swings on 30 ft cables through corners
components.dependence: Conditional on c1. This is a separate failure mode (lateral control, not forward traction).
components.reasoning: Granting c1, a swinging 20 t mass exerts lateral cable loads far above each car's lateral grip (about 17 kN). Every wide swing should drag both cars sideways. Staying on course through a city chase needs the swing to stay small at every corner; judged 1 in 100 to 1 in 100,000.

components.claim: Dom aims the swinging vault into specific targets
components.dependence: Conditional on c2 (the cars are controllable at all).
components.reasoning: A pendulum on a cable steered by one of two independently driven cars. Judgment prior around 1 in 10 per aimed hit.

components.reasoning: An An-124 makes about 900 kN of thrust and, near rotation speed, about 4 MN of lift. A car's braking or anchoring force is about 16 kN (0.9 x 1.8 t x g). components.claim: One arm, from a moving vehicle, turns a 2 t torpedo moving at about 50 mph
components.reasoning: Lateral impulse F = m x v x sin(theta) / t, with m = 2 t and v = 22 m/s. The four corners of 3-10 degrees over 0.5-1 s give 2.3 kN, 4.6 kN, 7.6 kN and 15.3 kN. The heaviest deadlift ever is about 5 kN with both legs and ideal footing; a one-arm pull while leaning from a moving vehicle is perhaps 1-1.5 kN. The requirement is therefore 1.5x to 15x the plausible force: marginal at the gentlest corner, far beyond it at the sharpest. It is not capped because the gentlest corner, which is the assumption most favourable to the stunt, stays under 3x. The wide MU range is deliberate.

components.claim: Grabbing the torpedo does not set it off, but hitting the target vehicle does
components.reasoning: Contact fuzes are built to fire on impacts far softer than a car collision; the ice skid, the grab and the hit form a narrow sequence. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

components.claim: Driving fast enough to be clear of a pressure-triggered mine before it explodes
components.dependence: First component; one component for all cars (the mines are the same type).
components.reasoning: Anti-vehicle mines fire within milliseconds of pressure; at 80 mph (36 m/s) a car moves about 4 cm per millisecond. Getting about 5 m clear needs a fuze delay of about 140 ms, which standard pressure fuzes do not have. Speed only helps if every mine in the field has an unusual delay. Judged 1 in 100 to 1 in 100,000.

components.claim: Roman escapes a mine blast that destroys his car
components.dependence: Conditional on c1 failing locally for Roman's car (the mine catches his car but not him).
components.reasoning: Anti-vehicle mines are designed to kill a vehicle's occupants. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

ev-ff09-01.depicted: Fleeing soldiers, the team drives into a minefield. Tej tells everyone to stay above 80 mph "to avoid being blown up"; they race through as mines detonate around them. Roman's car is destroyed and he barely escapes the blast.
ev-ff09-01.title: Outrunning landmines at 80 mph
visually_unverified: whether mines detonate behind or under the cars

components.claim: A car driven off a cliff snags a dangling rope so that it is securely attached
components.reasoning: The rope must catch on a part of the car that holds (not slide off the bodywork). Judgment prior about 1 in 30.

components.claim: A single old bridge rope holds a 2 t car at the bottom of the swing
components.reasoning: Tension at the bottom of the swing is m(g + v2/L): with v = 20-30 m/s and L = 30 m that is 2 t x 23-40 m/s2 = 46-80 kN, before the shock load of the catch. A weathered natural-fibre rope of this size breaks at roughly 10-40 kN. The requirement is 2-8x the rope's strength. Judged 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 100 million.

components.claim: The swing releases the car onto the far cliff rather than into its face
components.reasoning: A pendulum returns to its release height only at the same side unless the pivot and timing work out. Judged about 1 in 10.

ev-ff09-02.depicted: With the rope bridge collapsed, Dom drives his Charger off the cliff toward its remains, snags a rope from the bridge, swings across on it and lands on the far cliffside.
ev-ff09-02.inferred: The bridge had just carried Tej's Jeep before collapsing. The Fandom sequence page puts Letty in Dom's Charger for this jump, after she is thrown from her motorcycle in the minefield.
ev-ff09-02.title: Charger swings across the gorge on the bridge's rope

components.claim: An aircraft magnet catches and carries a 1.7 t car
components.reasoning: Industrial lifting magnets hold cars from above, but only when stationary and in contact. Catching a moving car in flight adds a jolt several times the car's weight, and heavy-lift drones do not carry 1.7 t. Held at the judgment cap because the vehicle type is disputed.

components.claim: Jakob survives the snatch jolt uninjured
components.reasoning: Depends on the relative speed at capture, which is unknown. Judgment prior about 1 in 3.

ev-ff09-03.depicted: Cornered at a cliff edge with the device, Jakob is picked up, car and all, by a large aircraft or drone with a magnet underneath.
ev-ff09-03.inferred: Sources disagree on drone vs plane and on whether he has already driven off the cliff.
ev-ff09-03.title: Jakob and his car snatched by a magnet aircraft
visually_unverified: whether the car is already falling

components.claim: A truck-mounted electromagnet pulls a driving car across a gap of metres
components.reasoning: Magnetic pull on steel falls off steeply with distance (roughly the fourth power for a dipole), which is why scrapyard magnets work only at contact. Out-pulling a car's own traction (about 15 kN) from metres away would need a magnet of MRI-plus scale on a truck. Judged at the judgment cap because the field is unspecified.

ev-ff09-04.depicted: Ramsey, driving the villains' electromagnet truck, uses its magnet to pull Jakob's escaping car toward them.
ev-ff09-04.inferred: Field strength and distance are not given.
ev-ff09-04.title: Truck electromagnet hauls in a car

components.claim: Cars of about 2 t each flip an armoured truck many times their mass
components.reasoning: A magnet only pulls the car and the truck together; any upward force on the truck must be reacted by the car's weight and traction, a small fraction of the truck's. A flip could only come from the truck's own momentum being redirected. Without a known mechanism this is held at the judgment cap.

ev-ff09-05.depicted: The team magnetises their cars to the front of Otto's armoured 16-wheeler, the "Armadillo", and with Jakob's help sends it flipping upwards, end over end, out of the city.
ev-ff09-05.inferred: The exact mechanism is not described in either source.
ev-ff09-05.title: Magnetised cars flip an armoured truck out of Tbilisi

components.claim: The rocket bolted to a Fiero delivers about 9 km/s of delta-v
components.reasoning: Orbit needs 9.3-9.8 km/s from the ground; the 15 km air launch saves only a few hundred m/s. Even at a generous 300 s specific impulse the rocket equation needs a mass ratio of about 21, i.e. about 30 t of propellant for a 1.5 t vehicle. The tanks shown hold well under 1 t. The shortfall is more than 30x, a hard limit; capped.

components.claim: A car body with bolted fins survives supersonic ascent without tumbling or breaking up
components.dependence: Conditional on c1. A separate failure mode (stability and structure, not propellant).
components.reasoning: Given c1, a car is aerodynamically unstable (centre of pressure ahead of centre of mass) and not built for the loads at maximum dynamic pressure. Real rockets need active guidance to stay pointed. Judged 1 in 100 to 1 in 100,000.

components.claim: Two men survive vacuum in duct-taped wetsuits and scuba helmets
components.dependence: Conditional on c2; one component for both men (same improvised design).
components.reasoning: Above the Armstrong limit (19 km) a suit must hold a stable internal pressure over the whole body. A wetsuit is not a pressure garment; one leak means ebullism and unconsciousness in seconds. Both suits must hold for the whole flight. Judged 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 1,000,000.

components.claim: A hand-flown ascent intercepts one specific satellite on the first attempt
components.reasoning: Orbital rendezvous needs matched plane, altitude, phase and velocity. Gemini-era crews did it with onboard computers and ground tracking; a single launch window with manual control is judged 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 1,000,000.

components.claim: After ramming the satellite, the unpowered car drifts to the International Space Station
components.dependence: Conditional on c4. Separate from c4 because the satellite's orbit is not the ISS's orbit.
components.reasoning: Reaching the ISS needs the same orbital plane (a plane change costs km/s) and a near match in altitude, phase and velocity. The chance that an arbitrary orbit after a collision passes within reach of the ISS with a matched velocity is far below one in a trillion (the orbital shell alone is ~2e10 km3). Capped.

ev-ff09-06.depicted: Tej and Roman ride a rocket-powered Pontiac Fiero dropped from a carrier aircraft at 50,000 ft. They reach orbit in duct-taped, wetsuit-like suits with scuba-style helmets. When the car's magnet fails, they ram the Aries satellite and destroy it, then drift to the International Space Station, whose crew spots them and brings them back to Earth.
ev-ff09-06.inferred: One recap says the launch platform is a drone; three say a plane at 50,000 ft.
ev-ff09-06.title: Pontiac Fiero goes to space

components.claim: A truck thrown by a missile blast hits the aircraft that fired it
components.reasoning: The blast throws the truck in a direction set by the blast geometry; the drone must be low and on that line at that moment. Judged 1 in 10 to 1 in 1,000.

components.claim: Dom leaps from the truck a moment before the missile hits and is unhurt
components.reasoning: Jumping from a moving truck next to a missile strike. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

ev-ff09-07.depicted: Cipher fires at the armoured truck from a drone jet. Dom jumps out at the last moment, Otto dies, and the blast sends the truck into Cipher's drone, destroying it.
ev-ff09-07.title: Blast-thrown truck swats Cipher's drone
visually_unverified: height of the drone at impact

components.claim: A car steers a free-rolling multi-ton sphere along chosen city streets by pushing it
components.reasoning: Pushing a sphere with a flat bumper is unstable; the ball deflects sideways at every contact, and the Charger weighs the same as the ball or much less. Steering it over a planned route is judged about 1 in 100.

components.claim: The armed bomb survives impacts, stairs and car strikes without detonating early
components.reasoning: An armed device taking repeated heavy shocks. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

components.claim: Dom survives a city-scale blast at the river's edge
components.dependence: Conditional on c1 (he is at the river when it goes in).
components.reasoning: He pushes the bomb in and drives away; a blast wave travels at the speed of sound or faster, far faster than a car, so survival depends only on the distance he reached. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

ev-ff10-01.depicted: Dante releases a giant spherical bomb that rolls through Rome, crushing cars, splitting a bus and bouncing down the Spanish Steps. Dom uses his Charger to push it through the streets, then drives into a crane that knocks it into the Tiber, limiting the damage when it detonates.
ev-ff10-01.inferred: The bomb's in-story mass is unclear (the prop was one ton; one article calls it ten).
ev-ff10-01.title: Steering a rolling bomb through Rome into the Tiber
visually_unverified: how far Dom is from the blast

components.claim: Dom walks away from a car landing after a 15-60 m drop at aircraft speed
components.reasoning: A 15 m drop lands at 17 m/s vertical (38 mph), walk-away 0.4 MU on the NHTSA curve; a 60 m drop lands at 34 m/s (76 mph), 2.7 MU (extrapolated above the curve's 60 mph fit). The range covers the height uncertainty.

components.claim: The car is still drivable after landing at 17-34 m/s vertical plus aircraft ground speed
components.reasoning: Production jump cars break suspension at a fraction of this landing speed; a car that lands at highway speed from this height and keeps driving is judged about 1 in 100.

ev-ff10-02.depicted: Dom arrives with Aimes aboard a plane and drops his Charger out of it onto the highway below, landing and driving straight into the chase.
ev-ff10-02.inferred: One review puts the drop at "200+ feet"; the plane must fly at least around 60 m/s to stay airborne.
ev-ff10-02.title: Charger dropped from a cargo plane onto the highway
visually_unverified: whether it lands on another car

components.claim: The car stays wheels-down on a near-vertical 140 m face instead of tumbling
components.reasoning: On a near-vertical face the tyres barely load, so steering is almost useless; judged about 1 in 10.

components.claim: Father and child survive a 140 m descent ending in water at about 50 m/s, and are functional
components.dependence: Conditional on c1; one component for both occupants.
components.reasoning: If braking fails on a face this steep (friction would need to exceed tan(slope)), the car reaches roughly sqrt(2gh) = 52 m/s at the bottom. Golden Gate data: a 75 m fall into water is survived about 2% of the time, with major injuries. A 140 m descent is worse (about 0.1-0.5% survival), and both are shown alive and alert. The car's frame and belts help somewhat.

ev-ff10-03.depicted: Boxed in between two drone-driven tanker trucks on top of a dam, Dom drives off the edge with his son Little B, down the dam's face, and lands in the water below. Both are shown alive before Dante blows up the dam.
ev-ff10-03.inferred: The real Aldeadávila Dam is 460 ft; the director described it as a "vertical quarter mile".
ev-ff10-03.title: Driving down the face of a 460 ft dam
visually_unverified: slope of the face as depicted

components.claim: Mid-fall, in a few seconds, she forces a grown man underneath her and stays on top at impact
components.reasoning: Everyone in a falling car is weightless, so nobody has footing, and winning the positioning struggle in the few seconds available is judged about 1 in 10. No written source describes her protecting herself; the human-cushion mechanism rests on the owner's viewing confirmation, and one recap instead says the henchman is impaled on a pipe at the bottom of the shaft.

components.claim: A body under her turns a free-fall elevator impact into a survivable one
components.reasoning: Inside a falling car she hits the floor at the car's own impact speed. A body beneath adds only about 20-30 cm of stopping distance, a modest cut in peak deceleration. Real elevator free-fall survivors exist (shaft buffers and air cushioning help), so this is not impossible. Held at the judgment cap because the height is unknown.

ev-ff10-04.depicted: Trapped in an elevator with a henchman Dante has turned against her, Cipher shoots out the car's cable. The car free-falls to the bottom of the shaft; she positions the henchman beneath her as a crash cushion. He dies; she survives and reaches Dom's house, wounded, that night.
ev-ff10-04.inferred: The shaft height is not given.
ev-ff10-04.title: Cipher rides a free-falling elevator down on a human cushion

components.claim: A small aircraft leaves an airliner's cargo hold in flight and flies clear of the airliner
components.reasoning: A cargo hatch opened in flight exposes the hold to an airstream moving at the airliner's speed, and a light aircraft released into it must separate without striking the fuselage or tail. No source gives the altitude, the speed or the hatch type, so no force comparison is possible and the component is held at the judgment cap.

components.claim: Three miniature bottles of vodka usefully fuel the aircraft
components.reasoning: Three miniatures hold about 60 ml of ethanol, a tiny fraction of the fuel any powered aircraft carries. If the aircraft is a glider the fuel matters less, which is why the range is wide. Judgment prior about 1 in 100.

components.claim: A man and a child stay conscious and uninjured in a small open aircraft leaving cruise flight
components.dependence: Conditional on c1; one component for both occupants.
components.reasoning: At airliner cruise altitude the air is too thin to stay conscious for long and very cold. The altitude is not established by two sources, so this is judged, about 1 in 10.

ev-ff10-05.depicted: A flight attendant gives Jakob a key and three miniature bottles of vodka. He fights off the agents sent after him and Little B, and the two leave the airliner mid-flight in a small aircraft stowed in the cargo hold, with the alcohol used as fuel.
ev-ff10-05.inferred: Sources disagree on the aircraft: a glider in some recaps, a jet in others. Single sources give the key opening the cargo hatch, a 747 and 36,000 ft; none of these is used as a fact.
ev-ff10-05.title: Escaping an airliner mid-flight in a small aircraft from the cargo hold

components.claim: While harpooned from both sides, Dom drives so that the two helicopters collide with each other
components.reasoning: The helicopters fly on opposite sides of the road, and one jump must pull both onto the same line at the same moment. Judgment prior about 1 in 100.

components.claim: Dom and the car survive the drop from the upper deck to the lower deck and keep driving
components.reasoning: In production an empty Charger fired from the top deck onto the lower deck was wrecked beyond repair. A driver walking away and the car still running is judged about 1 in 10.

components.claim: A car spinning donuts swings two tethered helicopter wrecks as flails
components.reasoning: Each wreck is likely heavier than the car, so a spinning car would be dragged by the wrecks rather than swing them. The helicopter model is not named, so no mass comparison is possible and the component is held at the judgment cap.

ev-ff10-06.depicted: Two helicopters fire harpoons on cables into Dom's Charger to lift it off an elevated highway. Dom fires the nitrous and jumps from the upper deck to the lower deck, and the tethered helicopters collide and crash. He then spins the car and swings the burning wrecks, still attached by cable, into Dante's cars.
ev-ff10-06.inferred: No source names the helicopter model or gives the cable length, the deck height or the speed. The production did not film a real collision or real cables.
ev-ff10-06.title: Two harpoon helicopters made to collide, then swung as flails
visually_unverified: whether the collision is caused by the jump or by the speed burst

components.claim: Dom makes a moving car roll in the one way that throws a bomb clear
components.reasoning: Rolling another car deliberately is uncontrolled, and the bomb must come off rather than stay attached. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

components.claim: The bomb comes free before Dante detonates it
components.reasoning: Dante is already moving to detonate it, so the window is seconds long. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

components.claim: Isabel survives a racing rollover

ev-ff10-07.depicted: Dante has planted bombs on Isabel's and Diogo's cars. After Diogo's car explodes, Dante moves to detonate Isabel's. Dom makes her car crash and roll, which knocks the bomb off, and he pulls her out of the wreck.

components.claim: A child jumps between two cars at highway speed and lands inside through a window
components.reasoning: Professional stunt performers do car-to-car transfers with rigging and rehearsal. A child doing it unrigged, through a window, is judged about 1 in 30.

components.claim: Dom holds his car level with Dante's, close enough for the jump, under fire
components.reasoning: The gap and speed must match for the second the jump takes. Judgment prior about 1 in 10.

ev-ff10-08.depicted: Dante has grabbed Little B into his car. Dom pulls alongside at speed, and Little B jumps out of Dante's car and in through the Charger's window.

components.claim: One man defeats a prepared armed team without being disabled
components.reasoning: Scored against real-world conditions; the cybernetic excuse is tagged, not credited. Small-unit engagements where one attacker defeats a whole armed team are rare. Judgment prior around 1 in 100, at the judgment cap.

ev-hs-01.title: Brixton defeats an entire MI6 team alone

components.claim: A runner controls his speed down a glass face far steeper than 45 degrees
components.reasoning: To descend without accelerating, friction must exceed tan(slope): 1.0 at 45 degrees and 5.7 at 80 degrees. Shoe rubber on glass gives about 0.5-1.0. Stronger legs do not change friction, so on any face steep enough to look like a skyscraper he is sliding at close to free fall. Hard limit; capped. Low confidence because the on-screen angle is not measured.

ev-hs-02.depicted: Brixton grabs Hattie, exits a high window, and runs down the steeply slanted exterior face of the tower to street level.
ev-hs-02.inferred: The filming reference is the 225 m Leadenhall Building, whose one face slants like a wedge.
ev-hs-02.title: Brixton runs down a skyscraper's slanted face carrying Hattie

components.claim: A 118 kg man descends a tower by jumping between moving human footholds
components.reasoning: Each landing on a suspended person must hold a large man's impact load, several times in a row. Judgment prior around 1 in 100.

components.claim: Hobbs survives the descent and the crash through plate glass uninjured
components.reasoning: Glass lacerations and uncontrolled drops between footholds. Judgment prior around 1 in 10.

ev-hs-03.depicted: Hobbs jumps out of the same window after Brixton, descending the building by leaping from person to person, and tackles Brixton through plate glass.

ev-hs-03.title: Hobbs descends the tower by leaping onto people

components.claim: Shaw places a 1.2 m tall car under trailer decks of about the same height at speed
components.reasoning: A 720S is 1.196 m tall. Standard trailer decks sit about 1.2-1.3 m up, so the car fits only between the wheel sets and only if it stays centred. Judgment prior around 1 in 10.

components.claim: The gap under both crossing trailers is open at the moment the car arrives
components.reasoning: Two moving trailers must both present their open span during the fraction of a second the car passes. About 1 in 10.

ev-hs-04.depicted: Chased by Brixton's motorcycles, Shaw drives the McLaren 720S under two crossing articulated lorries with minimal clearance.
ev-hs-04.title: McLaren threads under two crossing lorries

components.claim: A chained convoy of trucks holds a Black Hawk and the pilot keeps control with a tether attached
components.reasoning: This part is roughly plausible. The Black Hawk's excess lift is about 20-40 kN, and a 9 t truck resists about 90 kN. The real risk is dynamic rollover from a side-pulling tether, which pilots train to avoid. Judged about 1 in 10.

components.claim: One man holds a helicopter that is pulling with 20-40 kN
components.dependence: Conditional on c1 (the helicopter is tethered and flyable when the chain breaks).
components.reasoning: The heaviest deadlift ever is 510 kg, about 5 kN, lifted with legs, a bar and ideal footing. The helicopter's excess lift is 4-8x that, and friction under Hobbs's feet is only about 1 kN. Hard limit; capped.

ev-hs-05.depicted: The Hobbs family chains a convoy of trucks to Brixton's UH-60 Black Hawk in a cliffside tug-of-war. When the chain breaks, Hobbs grabs it and holds the helicopter back with his own strength.
ev-hs-05.inferred: The chain was CGI and the cliffside road is a constructed, composited set. The helicopter and the trucks were largely practical (the director says about 95%).
ev-hs-05.title: Hobbs holds a Black Hawk by its chain
visually_unverified: whether Hobbs is braced or anchored
